note: Bundled public-claim corpus covering Meta AI safety. Each item is a paraphrase or short quote of a PUBLIC statement with its source URL. Covers Meta's Responsible Use Guide, Llama model cards, and Meta AI safety blog. Verify against sources before citing externally.

claims.text: Meta's Responsible Use Guide for Llama models defines permitted and prohibited uses, including hard prohibitions on using Llama for weapons of mass destruction, critical infrastructure attacks, malware generation, and CBRN uplift.

Meta releases Llama models with publicly available system cards documenting red-team evaluation results, known capability limitations, fine-tuning risks, and safety mitigations including safety-tuned RLHF variants.

Meta's Llama 3 purple-teaming effort included testing for CBRN uplift, cyberattack assistance, jailbreak susceptibility, and code generation for malicious purposes; safety mitigations were updated in response.
Meta maintains a Bug Bounty program for AI systems and accepts responsible-disclosure reports for harmful content generation vulnerabilities across Meta AI products.
Meta publishes an annual 'Responsible AI Report' documenting progress on Responsible AI principles across fairness, transparency, privacy, safety, and accountability.

Meta's open-release model policy is governed by a responsible-release checklist; models above certain capability thresholds receive restricted access rather than open weights, as stated in Meta's dual-use risk analysis process.

Meta AI's agentic tools (Meta AI with tool access, AI agents in products) apply usage-policy controls on actions, documented in Meta's AI-integrated product policies, with human-visible disclosure of AI-generated content.
